categoryMeta.description: 3K and 5K workouts including VO2max, threshold, race pace, and sharpening sessions.

workouts.title: 5K Run-Walk Foundations
workouts.summary: A gentle run-walk progression to safely establish aerobic foundation and cardiovascular conditioning for 5K running.
workouts.riskReason: Time-based alternating intervals keep physical impact low, minimizing calf, shin, and tendon impact.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run at an easy RPE 4 effort. You should be able to speak full sentences easily during the running blocks.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate remains in low aerobic zones; ensure it settles fully during the walking recoveries.

warmup.name: Aerobic Warmup Walk-Jog
warmup.description: 800m continuous easy progressive walk and light jog (RPE 3) to prepare joints.

warmup.name: Light Activation Exercises
warmup.description: Dynamic leg swings, hip extensions, and ankle rotations (5 mins) to prepare leg muscles.

mainSet.name: Run-Walk Intervals
mainSet.description: Run 2 minutes at conversational effort, then walk 1 minute for recovery. Maintain slow, controlled movements.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce to 8 repetitions of 90 seconds running / 90 seconds walking.

mainSet.name: Run-Walk Intervals (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 8 × (90s run / 90s walk) at easy RPE 4 effort.

harder.description: Increase to 12 repetitions to safely extend overall session volume.

mainSet.name: Run-Walk Intervals (Extended)
mainSet.description: 12 × (2 min run / 1 min walk) at easy RPE 4 effort.

coachingNotes: Resist the urge to run fast. Pacing consistency and conversational volume are the keys here.
Walk briskly during the recoveries to maintain cardiorespiratory circulation.
Focus on landing with a flat, midfoot strike.
commonMistakes: Running the 2-minute blocks at 5K race pace, leading to local lactic fatigue and heavy breathing.
Sitting down or standing completely still during the walking recovery.
safetyNotes: Pay attention to early signs of shin splints. Run on soft grass or turf if available.
Ensure your running shoes fit comfortably to prevent blister friction.
Stop immediately if you experience sharp knee or hip pain.

shareCard.purposeText: Build joint stamina and baseline aerobic capacity safely.
shareCard.footerNote: Flat grass or turf surfaces highly recommended.

workouts.sourceNote: Foundational walk-run programming for new athletes.

workouts.title: Continuous Aerobic Introduction
workouts.summary: A continuous conversational run designed to establish aerobic durability and pacing consistency over a sustained duration.
workouts.riskReason: Steady, slow aerobic velocity keeps bone impact low, minimizing tendon shear stress.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Maintain a steady, slow aerobic tempo (RPE 4-5). Breathe fully through your nose if possible.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Keep heart rate stable in your personal aerobic zone (under 75% max HR).

warmup.name: Aerobic Warmup Walk-Jog
warmup.description: 800m continuous easy progressive walk and light jog (RPE 3) to prepare joints.

warmup.name: Light Activation Exercises
warmup.description: Dynamic leg swings, hip extensions, and ankle rotations (5 mins) to prepare leg muscles.

mainSet.name: 18-Min Continuous Aerobic Introduction
mainSet.description: Run 18 minutes continuously at an easy conversational aerobic effort.
notes: This is aerobic, not a tempo test.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce running duration to 15 minutes of continuous conversational running.

mainSet.name: Continuous Run (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 15 minutes of continuous easy running.

harder.description: Extend running duration to 25 minutes to build greater endurance.

mainSet.name: Continuous Run (Extended)
mainSet.description: 25 minutes of continuous easy running.

coachingNotes: Do not focus on speed. Pacing control is key; you should feel as comfortable at minute 20 as you did at minute 1.
Practice dynamic calf stretches dynamically before beginning.
Shake out your hands and arms every 5 minutes to stay loose.
commonMistakes: Running the first 5 minutes too fast, causing progressive breathing distress and stopping early.
Holding tension in the shoulders and jaw.
safetyNotes: Monitor shin bones for tenderness or dull aching post-run (indicative of early shin splints).
Keep posture tall to minimize lower back and hip compression.
Hydrate properly before the session, especially in warmer conditions.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific 5K aerobic durability and breathing control.
shareCard.footerNote: Perform on flat, low-impact paths.

workouts.title: Beginner Aerobic Ladder Fartlek
workouts.summary: A fun time-based ladder fartlek to introduce gentle pacing changes and neuromuscular speed play without track fatigue.
workouts.riskReason: Short intervals at controlled moderate intensity minimize local muscular acidosis and tendon load.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Surge at a moderate effort (RPE 5-6, slightly faster than normal easy run). Return to an easy recovery jog between surges.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate rises moderately during surges but should drop back to low aerobic zones during recovery.

warmup.name: Aerobic Warmup Walk-Jog
warmup.description: 800m continuous easy progressive walk and light jog (RPE 3) to prepare joints.

warmup.name: Light Activation Exercises
warmup.description: Dynamic leg swings, hip extensions, and ankle rotations (5 mins) to prepare leg muscles.

mainSet.name: Ladder Fartlek Surges
mainSet.description: Execute the following time-based surges at moderate effort, followed by equal duration easy recovery jogs: 1 min, 2 min, 3 min, 2 min, 1 min.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce the ladder height: surge 1 min, 2 min, 2 min, 1 min with 2 minutes of walking recovery.

mainSet.name: Ladder Fartlek Surges (Reduced)
mainSet.description: Surges of 1 min, 2 min, 2 min, 1 min at RPE 5. Walk recoveries.

harder.description: Increase target intensity during the final 2-minute and 1-minute surges to target 5K race pace effort.

mainSet.name: Ladder Fartlek Surges (Harder Pacing)
mainSet.description: Time-based surges: 1 min, 2 min, 3 min (moderate), 2 min, 1 min (5K pace effort). Equal recovery jog.

coachingNotes: This is speed-play! Enjoy the changes of pace and don't obsess over exact GPS pacing values.
Ensure your posture remains tall during surges: think 'hips high' and drive forward.
Breathe rhythmically; match breathing to your stride frequency.
commonMistakes: Treating the surges as maximal sprints, leading to complete physical breakdown and walking during recovery.
Skipping the dynamic activation drills.
safetyNotes: Be highly aware of foot placement if running on grass or uneven trails to avoid ankle twisting.
Monitor shin bones or calf tendons closely under progressive pace adjustments.
Ensure you land directly under your center of mass.

shareCard.mainSetText: Surge 1 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 1 Min | Equal Easy Jog Recovery
shareCard.purposeText: Introduce progressive speed adjustments and cadence play safely.
shareCard.footerNote: Can be run on rolling grass or smooth park paths.

workouts.title: Beginner 5K Sustained Builder
workouts.summary: A progressive sustained aerobic session designed to safely transition recreational runners toward full 5K distance endurance.
workouts.riskReason: Steady-state aerobic pace minimizes muscular strain and limits rapid biomechanical breakdown.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Start very easy (RPE 3-4), gradually building over the final 10 minutes to a steady moderate pace (RPE 5). Focus on postural control.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Maintain a comfortable, steady heart rate; check that breathing remains conversational.

warmup.name: Aerobic Warmup Walk-Jog
warmup.description: 800m continuous easy progressive walk and light jog (RPE 3) to prepare joints.

warmup.name: Light Activation Exercises
warmup.description: Dynamic leg swings, hip extensions, and ankle rotations (5 mins) to prepare leg muscles.

mainSet.name: Progressive Sustained Run
mainSet.description: Run 25 minutes continuous. The first 15 mins at easy conversational pace, final 10 mins at progressive moderate pace.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce to 20 minutes continuous easy conversational running.

mainSet.name: Progressive Sustained Run (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 20 minutes continuous easy running at RPE 4.

harder.description: Extend continuous running to 30 minutes to challenge endurance.

mainSet.name: Progressive Sustained Run (Extended)
mainSet.description: 30 minutes continuous progressive running at RPE 4-5.

coachingNotes: Think about running with 'light feet'—minimize ground contact noise.
Keep your chin level and gaze looking 15-20 meters ahead.
Excellent session to build psychological confidence for the full 5K distance.
commonMistakes: Starting the session too fast, turning it into a tempo race instead of a base builder.
Letting the hips drop or slouching under early fatigue.
safetyNotes: Shin splints and Achilles stiffness are risks when progressive volume increases. Listen to your body.
Always stretch your calves and Achilles post-run.
Decelerate to a slow walk gradually when finishing the 25 minutes.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific muscular endurance and psychological pacing confidence.
shareCard.footerNote: Best run on flat park paths or paved trails.

workouts.sourceNote: Aerobic stamina principles to safely bridge beginner and intermediate training.

workouts.title: Cruise Interval Foundations
workouts.summary: A foundational threshold interval session utilizing short rest periods to accumulate time at lactate threshold safely.
workouts.riskReason: Sustained high aerobic loads can cause calves and shins to tighten if strides are tense.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run 1200 meters at a controlled, comfortable hard effort (RPE 6-7). This is your 10K/half-marathon effort.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high aerobic zone (approx 80-85% max HR).

warmup.name: Cardiorespiratory Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1200m easy jog at conversational pace (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: Lower Leg & Hip Activation
warmup.description: 5 mins dynamic stretching followed by leg swings, high knees, butt kicks, and walking lunges.

warmup.name: Rhythmic Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 3 × 800m/1K race pace strides (approx 60-80m), building progressive acceleration. Walk back recovery.

mainSet.name: Cruise Threshold Reps
mainSet.description: Run 1200 meters at controlled lactate threshold effort. Rest exactly 90 seconds walking/jogging between reps.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce to 3 repetitions with 2 minutes of walking recovery.

mainSet.name: Cruise Threshold Reps (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 3 × 1200m at threshold pace. 120 seconds recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 5 repetitions to challenge specific aerobic stamina.

mainSet.name: Cruise Threshold Reps (Extended)
mainSet.description: 5 × 1200m at threshold pace. 90 seconds recovery.

coachingNotes: Lactate threshold is 'comfortably hard'—not gasping or all-out.
Keep recovery blocks strictly timed at 90 seconds to prevent full clearance, training the body to clear lactate actively.
Run tall and smooth.
commonMistakes: Running the first 400m at 5K race pace, leading to heavy breathing and muscle burn.
Extending recovery jog duration too long.
safetyNotes: Lactate threshold work is low-risk but requires solid dynamic warmup to avoid calf strains.
Monitor shin bones or ankle joints if running on hard concrete roads.
Ensure proper cool down flushing.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate buffering capacity and pacing discipline.
shareCard.footerNote: Paved path or track track recommended.

workouts.sourceNote: Classic Jack Daniels threshold interval methodology.

workouts.title: Continuous Threshold Endurance
workouts.summary: A continuous tempo run designed to train the mind and body to maintain a steady, controlled state of high aerobic output.
workouts.riskReason: Continuous high aerobic output can place stress on the lower leg muscles (calves, shins) if posture slouches under fatigue.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run continuously at your lactate threshold (RPE 6-7). You should be able to speak short phrases only.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high aerobic zone (approx 80-85% max HR).

warmup.name: Cardiorespiratory Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1200m easy jog at conversational pace (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: Lower Leg & Hip Activation
warmup.description: 5 mins dynamic stretching followed by leg swings, high knees, butt kicks, and walking lunges.

warmup.name: Rhythmic Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 3 × 800m/1K race pace strides (approx 60-80m), building progressive acceleration. Walk back recovery.

mainSet.name: Continuous Tempo Run
mainSet.description: Run 20 minutes continuous. Keep the intensity stable; focus on high posture and smooth diaphragmatic breathing.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce tempo duration to 15 minutes continuous.

mainSet.name: Tempo Run (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 15 minutes continuous running at RPE 6-7.

harder.description: Extend tempo duration to 25 minutes continuous (Advanced capacity).

mainSet.name: Tempo Run (Extended)
mainSet.description: 25 minutes continuous running at RPE 6-7.

coachingNotes: Focus on nasal breathing for the first 10 minutes to help regulate effort.
Ensure you do not turn this into a race. Controlled pacing is far more beneficial than maximum speed.
Shake your arms out to release shoulder tension every mile.
commonMistakes: Running at 5K race pace, leading to hyperventilation and a premature stop before 20 minutes.
Tensing the jaw and shoulders.
safetyNotes: Continuous pounding on hard pavement increases shin splint risk. Choose flat park trails if possible.
Always stretch calf muscles and Achilles tendons post-run.
Ensure proper hydration before the run.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate clearance threshold and mental stamina.
shareCard.footerNote: Paved path or flat hard-pack dirt recommended.

workouts.title: Threshold Cruise Ladders
workouts.summary: An advanced, high-volume threshold session using progressive ladder repeats to build lactate capacity and event pacing flexibility.
workouts.riskReason: High-volume repetition loads can cause calf, hamstring, and shin fatigue if mechanics break down under extended distance.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run each ladder step at controlled threshold effort (RPE 7). Take exactly 75 seconds recovery jog.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Maintain a steady, controlled heart rate in high aerobic zones (approx 80-85% max HR).

warmup.name: Aerobic Priming Jog
warmup.description: 1600m progressive continuous jog, starting slow and ending at a steady moderate aerobic clip (RPE 4-5).

warmup.name: Dynamic Biomechanical Priming
warmup.description: 10 mins dynamic stretching, dynamic hip/groin drills, followed by A-skips, B-skips, and light lateral side-shuffles.

warmup.name: Race Pacing Priming Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 60m strides on flat straight track or turf, accelerating to target 5K/3K pace effort. Walk back recovery.

mainSet.name: Cruise Ladder 1K-1200m-1K-800m
mainSet.description: Run a controlled threshold ladder with easy jog recoveries.
notes: Keep effort even across the ladder.

cooldown.name: Extended Active Flush Jog
cooldown.description: 1200m very light recovery jog on grass or turf to reduce muscle stiffness and joint impact.

cooldown.name: Venous Return & Muscle Stretching
cooldown.description: 5 mins of legs elevated on a wall to facilitate metabolic clearance, followed by calf and Achilles stretching.

easier.description: Omit the 1600m rep, performing: 800m, 1200m, 1200m, 800m with 90 seconds recovery jog.

mainSet.name: Lactate Cruise Ladder (Reduced)
mainSet.description: Threshold reps: 800m, 1200m, 1200m, 800m. 90 seconds recovery jog.

harder.description: Decrease recovery jog duration to 60 seconds to push lactate buffering capabilities.

mainSet.name: Lactate Cruise Ladder (Extended)
mainSet.description: Threshold reps: 800m, 1200m, 1600m, 1200m, 800m with 60 seconds recovery jog.

coachingNotes: Pacing control is vital on the 1600m rep; settle into a smooth, relaxed rhythm early.
Keep recovery jogs structured; do not walk or stop completely to encourage active clearance.
Keep your jaw and shoulders relaxed.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the initial 800m at 5K race pace, leading to muscle lockup and failing the rest of the ladder.
Standing still during recovery jogs.
safetyNotes: High cumulative volume requires thorough dynamic warmups.
Calves and Achilles tendons are loaded extensively; wear supportive shoes.
Perform the extended legs-up cooldown flushes.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate clearance and pacing endurance under high volume.
shareCard.footerNote: Track or smooth flat path recommended.

workouts.sourceNote: High-volume ladder workouts for competitive road racers.

workouts.title: Mona Fartlek Adapted Threshold
workouts.summary: A continuous fartlek session adapting the legendary 'Mona' structure to build threshold clearance and speed-endurance.
workouts.riskReason: Continuous pace adjustments demand strong eccentric calf control and hamstring flexibility.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Surge at threshold effort (RPE 7) during hard segments, returning immediately to an easy float jog (RPE 5) during recoveries. No walking.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate remains elevated throughout; floats teach the cardiorespiratory system active recovery.

warmup.name: Cardiorespiratory Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1200m easy jog at conversational pace (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: Lower Leg & Hip Activation
warmup.description: 5 mins dynamic stretching followed by leg swings, high knees, butt kicks, and walking lunges.

warmup.name: Rhythmic Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 3 × 800m/1K race pace strides (approx 60-80m), building progressive acceleration. Walk back recovery.

mainSet.name: Modified Mona Threshold Fartlek
mainSet.description: Run a controlled threshold fartlek with varied rep lengths and relaxed floats.
notes: Do not turn the floats into hard running.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Omit the 90-second segments, performing: 4 × 60s, 4 × 30s, 4 × 15s with equal duration easy walk recoveries.

mainSet.name: Adapted Mona Set (Reduced)
mainSet.description: Continuous segments: 4 × 60s, 4 × 30s, 4 × 15s. Equal duration easy walk recoveries.

harder.description: Increase the surge segments intensity to target 5K race pace (RPE 8) while maintaining the easy float recovery jogs.

mainSet.name: Adapted Mona Set (Race Pace)
mainSet.description: Mona segments at 5K race pace (RPE 8) with easy float recovery jogs: 2 × 90s, 4 × 60s, 4 × 30s, 4 × 15s.

coachingNotes: The secret of Mona Fartlek is the float recovery. Do not jog extremely slow; keep it steady to clear lactate under load.
This adapted session is excellent to prepare for road race terrain changes.
Maintain high cadence during the shorter 30s and 15s surges.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the 90s segments at 3K/sprint pace, leading to complete recovery collapse and walking.
Walking during the recovery float jogs.
safetyNotes: Fast foot turnover changes demand supple calf muscles and Achilles tendons. Stretch calves thoroughly.
Run on flat, reliable park paths or paved surfaces.
Perform standard cool down stretching.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific active lactate clearance and neuromuscular pacing play.
shareCard.footerNote: Flat road or park loops recommended.

workouts.sourceNote: Adapted from legendary Australian marathoner Steve Moneghetti's training.

workouts.title: Aerobic Threshold Tempo Blocks
workouts.summary: A structured threshold session breaking up a continuous tempo run into two blocks to maintain high pacing quality and technical posture.
workouts.riskReason: Continuous high aerobic efforts place steady stress on calves and Achilles; breaking into blocks mitigates early fatigue collapse.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run each 10-minute block at a controlled threshold effort (RPE 6-7). Settle into a smooth breathing rhythm.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high aerobic zone; ensure it drops during the active jog recovery between sets.

warmup.name: Cardiorespiratory Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1200m easy jog at conversational pace (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: Lower Leg & Hip Activation
warmup.description: 5 mins dynamic stretching followed by leg swings, high knees, butt kicks, and walking lunges.

warmup.name: Rhythmic Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 3 × 800m/1K race pace strides (approx 60-80m), building progressive acceleration. Walk back recovery.

mainSet.name: Tempo Blocks
mainSet.description: Run 10 minutes at controlled threshold effort, rest 3 minutes with an easy jog, then run a second 10 minutes at threshold effort.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce block durations to 8 minutes each with 3 minutes easy walking recovery.

mainSet.name: Tempo Blocks (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 2 × 8 minutes threshold tempo with 180 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase block durations to 12 minutes each to extend the specific training volume.

mainSet.name: Tempo Blocks (Extended)
mainSet.description: 2 × 12 minutes threshold tempo with 180 seconds jogging recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on posture during the second block: keep your chest open and shoulders relaxed.
Use the 3-minute jog recovery to refresh mentally; do not run too fast.
Keep your breathing steady and diaphragmatic.
commonMistakes: Treating the first block as a maximum effort race, forcing a slow or DNF second block.
Skipping the recovery jog and standing still.
safetyNotes: Choose flat trails or soft surfaces to limit calf and shin irritation.
Ensure proper warm up mobilization beforehand.
Stop immediately if sharp shin pain occurs.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate clearance capability with a mid-session posture reset.
shareCard.footerNote: Flat roads or trails recommended.

workouts.title: Progressive Lactate Threshold Run
workouts.summary: A continuous progressive run that gradually transitions from aerobic base pace to threshold effort to train smooth pacing adjustments.
workouts.riskReason: The progressive increase in speed shifts loading patterns toward higher eccentric force, stressing calves and Achilles.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Start very easy (RPE 3-4), gradually building speed every 5 minutes, ending the final 5 minutes at Threshold Effort (RPE 7).
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate climbs progressively, finishing in the high lactate threshold zone (approx 80-85% max HR).

warmup.name: Cardiorespiratory Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1200m easy jog at conversational pace (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: Lower Leg & Hip Activation
warmup.description: 5 mins dynamic stretching followed by leg swings, high knees, butt kicks, and walking lunges.

warmup.name: Rhythmic Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 3 × 800m/1K race pace strides (approx 60-80m), building progressive acceleration. Walk back recovery.

mainSet.name: Progressive Threshold Run
mainSet.description: Run 25 minutes continuous: first 10 mins easy (RPE 3-4), middle 10 mins moderate (RPE 5-6), final 5 mins at threshold effort (RPE 7).

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce progressive run duration to 20 minutes continuous.

mainSet.name: Progressive Run (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 20 minutes progressive running: 10 mins easy / 7 mins moderate / 3 mins threshold.

harder.description: Extend progressive run duration to 30 minutes continuous: 15 mins easy / 10 mins moderate / 5 mins threshold.

mainSet.name: Progressive Run (Extended)
mainSet.description: 30 minutes progressive running: 15 mins easy / 10 mins moderate / 5 mins threshold.

coachingNotes: Pacing control is vital; do not start building speed too early in the session.
The final 5 minutes require deep mental focus; establish a smooth, tall rhythm.
Shake out hands to release tension.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the middle 10 minutes, making it impossible to maintain a controlled threshold effort in the final 5 minutes.
Slouching posture as pace increases.
safetyNotes: Shin splints and Achilles stiffness are risks during progressive load adjustments. Focus on landing flat under hips.
Ensure dynamic mobility stretching beforehand.
Perform structured cool down flushing.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate clearance and pacing control.
shareCard.footerNote: Flat paths or roads recommended.

workouts.title: Over-Under Threshold Surges
workouts.summary: A challenging threshold session alternating sub-threshold and super-threshold efforts within the same repetition to push lactate buffering capabilities.
workouts.riskReason: Repetitive speed adjustments under progressive lactic load expose calves and hamstrings to high mechanical strain.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run each 1K repetition alternating: first 800m at threshold pace (RPE 6-7), surge final 200m at 5K race pace (RPE 8).
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate spikes during the 200m surge; recover actively during the 90 seconds walking recovery.

warmup.name: Aerobic Priming Jog
warmup.description: 1600m progressive continuous jog, starting slow and ending at a steady moderate aerobic clip (RPE 4-5).

warmup.name: Dynamic Biomechanical Priming
warmup.description: 10 mins dynamic stretching, dynamic hip/groin drills, followed by A-skips, B-skips, and light lateral side-shuffles.

warmup.name: Race Pacing Priming Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 60m strides on flat straight track or turf, accelerating to target 5K/3K pace effort. Walk back recovery.

mainSet.name: Over-Under 1K Repetitions
mainSet.description: Perform 1K reps: 800m at controlled threshold pace, accelerate/surge final 200m to 5K race pace. Rest 90 seconds walking between reps.

cooldown.name: Extended Active Flush Jog
cooldown.description: 1200m very light recovery jog on grass or turf to reduce muscle stiffness and joint impact.

cooldown.name: Venous Return & Muscle Stretching
cooldown.description: 5 mins of legs elevated on a wall to facilitate metabolic clearance, followed by calf and Achilles stretching.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 2 minutes of walking recovery.

mainSet.name: Over-Under 1K Repetitions (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 1K reps (800m threshold / 200m 5K pace) with 120 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 6 repetitions with 90 seconds recovery jog (Strictly for highly conditioned runners).

mainSet.name: Over-Under 1K Repetitions (Extended)
mainSet.description: 6 × 1K reps (800m threshold / 200m 5K pace) with 90 seconds recovery jog.

coachingNotes: This over-under structure trains the body to clear lactate while running fast.
The 200m surge should be a smooth acceleration, not a maximal sprint.
Maintain high hips and tall posture down the final straightaway.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the 200m surge maximal speed, causing early lactic lockout.
Standing still or sitting down during the recovery.
safetyNotes: Thorough dynamic warmup is mandatory. Pay attention to early calf/hamstring soreness.
Ensure spikes are secure if using them on the track curve.
Ensure you perform the legs-up cooldown flushes.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate buffering and event-finish acceleration capabilities.
shareCard.footerNote: Track or flat marked path required.

workouts.title: VO2max 800m Classic Intervals
workouts.summary: A classic intermediate VO2max session utilizing 800m repetitions to safely elevate aerobic capacity and running economy.
workouts.riskReason: Sustained high-velocity running over 800m produces severe lactic fatigue, charging calves and hamstrings heavily.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run 800 meters at your current 5K race pace effort (RPE 8-9). Settle into a tall, smooth rhythm.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate rises to near max in final 200m; ensure it settles fully during the long walk-jog recovery.

warmup.name: Cardiorespiratory Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1200m easy jog at conversational pace (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: Lower Leg & Hip Activation
warmup.description: 5 mins dynamic stretching followed by leg swings, high knees, butt kicks, and walking lunges.

warmup.name: Rhythmic Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 3 × 800m/1K race pace strides (approx 60-80m), building progressive acceleration. Walk back recovery.

mainSet.name: 800m Classic Intervals
mainSet.description: Run 800 meters at controlled VO2max effort. Rest 3 minutes walking and jogging between reps.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Flush
cooldown.description: 800m very relaxed slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Targeted static stretches
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis anterior), hamstrings, and lower back.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 3.5 minutes of walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: 800m Classic Intervals (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 800m at VO2max effort with 210 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 6 repetitions with 2.5 minutes of walking recovery.

mainSet.name: 800m Classic Intervals (Extended)
mainSet.description: 6 × 800m at VO2max effort with 150 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: This is an aerobic capacity session, not a maximal sprint. Settle into a rhythm early.

Focus on shoulder posture: keep shoulders down and back, not hunched.
A 3-minute walking recovery is crucial to ensure high-quality speed work.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the first 800m too fast, causing rapid anaerobic lockout and a slow finish.
Standing still or sitting down during the recovery.
safetyNotes: Near-maximal speed over progressive distances produces extreme systemic lactic fatigue, high tendon forces, and acute pull risks under fatigue.
Always stretch calves, hamstrings, and Achilles tendons dynamically beforehand.
Stop immediately if sharp muscle pulling occurs.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific pacing consistency and movement economy.
shareCard.footerNote: Requires full track spikes and proper warmup.
